name: Barbell Back Squat
instructions: Brace 360°, sit between hips and knees, drive chest and hips up together.
setupTip: Setup: At Planet Fitness, use pre-loaded fixed barbells (20–60 lb) for curls/presses or auto-swap heavy compound barbell lifts to the Smith Machine or Leverage Machines.
steps: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack just above shoulder level. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder-width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times and maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees and sitting back with your hips as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until your hamstrings are on your calves. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel or middle of your foot as you straighten the legs and extend the hips to go back to the starting position.
formCues: Brace your core 360° before initiating each rep and keep spine/pelvis neutral.
Control descent for 2 seconds to full comfortable depth where target muscles stretch.
Drive evenly through your whole foot without letting knees cave inward.

Using half-reps with excessive weight instead of full controlled knee/hip range.

name: Barbell Front Squat
instructions: Keep elbows tall, torso upright, descend to full depth.
setupTip: Setup: At Planet Fitness, use pre-loaded fixed barbells (20–60 lb) for curls/presses or auto-swap heavy compound barbell lifts to the Smith Machine or Leverage Machines.
steps: To begin, first set the bar in a rack slightly below shoulder level. Rest the bar on top of the deltoids, pushing into the clavicles, and lightly touching the throat. Your hands should be in a clean grip, touching the bar only with your fingers to help keep it in position.

Lift the bar off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso. Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head and elbows up at all times. This will be your starting position.

Bend at the knees, sitting down between your legs. Continue down until your hamstrings are on your calves. Keep your knees aligned with your feet by consciously using your abductors to push your knees out as you squat.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor mainly with the heel or middle of your foot as you straighten the legs again and return to the starting position.

name: Hack Squat Machine
instructions: Shoulders snug under pads, lower back flat against pad, control the bottom.
setupTip: Machine Setup: Adjust seat height first so your working joint lines up with the machine's pivot marker, and use the drop-down 5 lb micro-weight for smooth overload.
steps: Place the back of your torso against the back pad of the machine and hook your shoulders under the shoulder pads provided.
Position your legs in the platform using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Tip: Keep your head up at all times and also maintain the back on the pad at all times.
Place your arms on the side handles of the machine and disengage the safety bars (which on most designs is done by moving the side handles from a facing front position to a diagonal position).

Now straighten your legs without locking the knees. This will be your starting position. (Note: For the purposes of this discussion we will use the medium stance described above which targets overall development; however you can choose any of the three stances described in the foot positioning section).

Begin to slowly lower the unit by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up (back on the pad at all times). Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calves becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: If you performed the exercise correctly, the front of the knees should make an imaginary straight line with the toes that is perpendicular to the front. If your knees are past that imaginary line (if they are past your toes) then you are placing undue stress on the knee and the exercise has been performed incorrectly.

name: Leg Press
instructions: Lower sled as deep as pelvis stays flat on seat; do not lock knees violently.
setupTip: Planet Fitness Tip: Always test safety catch release handles before your top set; keep your tailbone pressed firmly into the seat.
steps: Using a leg press machine, sit down on the machine and place your legs on the platform directly in front of you at a medium (shoulder width) foot stance. (Note: For the purposes of this discussion we will use the medium stance described above which targets overall development; however you can choose any of the three stances described in the foot positioning section).

Lower the safety bars holding the weighted platform in place and press the platform all the way up until your legs are fully extended in front of you. Tip: Make sure that you do not lock your knees. Your torso and the legs should make a perfect 90-degree angle. This will be your starting position.
As you inhale, slowly lower the platform until your upper and lower legs make a 90-degree angle.
Pushing mainly with the heels of your feet and using the quadriceps go back to the starting position as you exhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and ensure to lock the safety pins properly once you are done. You do not want that platform falling on you fully loaded.

instructions: Rear foot elevated, slight forward torso lean for glutes or upright for quads.

Begin by descending, flexing your knee and hip to lower your body down. Maintain good posture througout the movement. Keep the front knee in line with the foot as you perform the exercise.

name: Conventional Barbell Deadlift
instructions: Pull slack out of the bar, lats packed, push the floor away.
setupTip: Setup: At Planet Fitness, use pre-loaded fixed barbells (20–60 lb) for curls/presses or auto-swap heavy compound barbell lifts to the Smith Machine or Leverage Machines.
steps: Stand in front of a loaded barbell.

While keeping the back as straight as possible, bend your knees, bend forward and grasp the bar using a medium (shoulder width) overhand grip. This will be the starting position of the exercise. Tip: If it is difficult to hold on to the bar with this grip, alternate your grip or use wrist straps.

While holding the bar, start the lift by pushing with your legs while simultaneously getting your torso to the upright position as you breathe out. In the upright position, stick your chest out and contract the back by bringing the shoulder blades back. Think of how the soldiers in the military look when they are in standing in attention.

Go back to the starting position by bending at the knees while simultaneously leaning the torso forward at the waist while keeping the back straight. When the weights on the bar touch the floor you are back at the starting position and ready to perform another repetition.
Perform the amount of repetitions prescribed in the program.

instructions: Soft knee bend, push hips straight back until hamstrings reach full stretch.
setupTip: Setup: At Planet Fitness, use pre-loaded fixed barbells (20–60 lb) for curls/presses or auto-swap heavy compound barbell lifts to the Smith Machine or Leverage Machines.

Tip: Depending on the weight used, you may need wrist wraps to perform the exercise and also a raised platform in order to allow for better range of motion.
Bend the knees slightly and keep the shins vertical, hips back and back straight. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your back and arms completely straight at all times, use your hips to lift the bar as you exhale. Tip: The movement should not be fast but steady and under control.

Once you are standing completely straight up, lower the bar by pushing the hips back, only slightly bending the knees, unlike when squatting. Tip: Take a deep breath at the start of the movement and keep your chest up. Hold your breath as you lower and exhale as you complete the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

setupTip: Setup: At Planet Fitness, use pre-loaded fixed barbells (20–60 lb) for curls/presses or auto-swap heavy compound barbell lifts to the Smith Machine or Leverage Machines.
steps: Begin seated on the ground with a bench directly behind you. Have a loaded barbell over your legs. Using a fat bar or having a pad on the bar can greatly reduce the discomfort caused by this exercise.
Roll the bar so that it is directly above your hips, and lean back against the bench so that your shoulder blades are near the top of it.

Begin the movement by driving through your feet, extending your hips vertically through the bar. Your weight should be supported by your shoulder blades and your feet. Extend as far as possible, then reverse the motion to return to the starting position.

name: 45° Back Extension
instructions: Hinge around hip pad with neutral spine, squeeze glutes at top.
setupTip: Bodyweight Setup: Set a clean grip width, brace your abs and glutes into a rigid line, and own a controlled 2-second lowering phase on every rep.
steps: Lie face down on a hyperextension bench, tucking your ankles securely under the footpads.
Adjust the upper pad if possible so your upper thighs lie flat across the wide pad, leaving enough room for you to bend at the waist without any restriction.

With your body straight, cross your arms in front of you (my preference) or behind your head. This will be your starting position. Tip: You can also hold a weight plate for extra resistance in front of you under your crossed arms.

Start bending forward slowly at the waist as far as you can while keeping your back flat. Inhale as you perform this movement. Keep moving forward until you feel a nice stretch on the hamstrings and you can no longer keep going without a rounding of the back. Tip: Never round the back as you perform this exercise. Also, some people can go farther than others. The key thing is that you go as far as your body allows you to without rounding the back.

Slowly raise your torso back to the initial position as you inhale. Tip: Avoid the temptation to arch your back past a straight line. Also, do not swing the torso at any time in order to protect the back from injury.

name: Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Retract scapula, slight arch, touch lower sternum, press up and slightly back.
setupTip: Setup: At Planet Fitness, use pre-loaded fixed barbells (20–60 lb) for curls/presses or auto-swap heavy compound barbell lifts to the Smith Machine or Leverage Machines.
steps: Lie back on a flat bench. Using a medium width grip (a grip that creates a 90-degree angle in the middle of the movement between the forearms and the upper arms), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked. This will be your starting position.
From the starting position, breathe in and begin coming down slowly until the bar touches your middle chest.

After a brief pause, push the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out. Focus on pushing the bar using your chest muscles. Lock your arms and squeeze your chest in the contracted position at the top of the motion, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly again. Tip: Ideally, lowering the weight should take about twice as long as raising it.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.
formCues: Keep shoulder blades depressed and tucked back—never let shoulders shrug toward your ears.
Control the lowering (eccentric) phase for ~2 seconds into a comfortable deep stretch.
Drive smoothly to lockout while exhaling through the sticking point.
commonMistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom stretch or slamming the weight stack between reps.
Flaring elbows straight out at 90° instead of tucking ~30–45° in the scapular plane.

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
instructions: 30° bench angle, lower to upper chest/clavicle line with controlled tempo.
setupTip: Setup: At Planet Fitness, use pre-loaded fixed barbells (20–60 lb) for curls/presses or auto-swap heavy compound barbell lifts to the Smith Machine or Leverage Machines.
steps: Lie back on an incline bench. Using a medium-width grip (a grip that creates a 90-degree angle in the middle of the movement between the forearms and the upper arms), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, come down slowly until you feel the bar on you upper chest.

After a second pause, bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out and push the bar using your chest muscles. Lock your arms in the contracted position, squeeze your chest, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly again. Tip: it should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.

name: Flat Dumbbell Bench Press
instructions: 45° elbow tuck, lower dumbbells for deep pec stretch, press smoothly.
setupTip: Planet Fitness Dumbbells (5–75 lb): Clear floor space around your bench, plant both feet flat, and kick weights into position on your thighs before lying back.
steps: Lie down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand resting on top of your thighs. The palms of your hands will be facing each other.
Then, using your thighs to help raise the dumbbells up, lift the dumbbells one at a time so that you can hold them in front of you at shoulder width.

Once at shoulder width, rotate your wrists forward so that the palms of your hands are facing away from you. The dumbbells should be just to the sides of your chest, with your upper arm and forearm creating a 90 degree angle. Be sure to maintain full control of the dumbbells at all times. This will be your starting position.

Then, as you breathe out, use your chest to push the dumbbells up. Lock your arms at the top of the lift and squeeze your chest, hold for a second and then begin coming down slowly. Tip: Ideally, lowering the weight should take about twice as long as raising it.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions of your training program.

Drive smoothly to lockout while exhaling through the sticking point.

name: Incline Dumbbell Press

steps: Lie back on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand atop your thighs. The palms of your hands will be facing each other.
Then, using your thighs to help push the dumbbells up, lift the dumbbells one at a time so that you can hold them at shoulder width.
Once you have the dumbbells raised to shoulder width, rotate your wrists forward so that the palms of your hands are facing away from you. This will be your starting position.
Be sure to keep full control of the dumbbells at all times. Then breathe out and push the dumbbells up with your chest.

name: Machine Chest Press
instructions: Set seat so handles align with mid-chest, push close to failure safely.
setupTip: Planet Fitness Tip: Set the yellow seat lever so the handles line up with mid-chest (nipple line). Flip down the 5 lb / 7.5 lb add-on weight for smooth micro-jumps.
steps: Sit down on the Chest Press Machine and select the weight.
Step on the lever provided by the machine since it will help you to bring the handles forward so that you can grab the handles and fully extend the arms.

Grab the handles with a palms-down grip and lift your elbows so that your upper arms are parallel to the floor to the sides of your torso. Tip: Your forearms will be pointing forward since you are grabbing the handles. Once you bring the handles forward and extend the arms you will be at the starting position.
Now bring the handles back towards you as you breathe in.
Push the handles away from you as you flex your pecs and you breathe out. Hold the contraction for a second before going back to the starting position.

setupTip: Bodyweight Setup: Set a clean grip width, brace your abs and glutes into a rigid line, and own a controlled 2-second lowering phase on every rep.

While breathing in, lower yourself slowly with your torso leaning forward around 30 degrees or so and your elbows flared out slightly until you feel a slight stretch in the chest.
Once you feel the stretch, use your chest to bring your body back to the starting position as you breathe out. Tip: Remember to squeeze the chest at the top of the movement for a second.

steps: Lie on the floor face down and place your hands about 36 inches apart while holding your torso up at arms length.
Next, lower yourself downward until your chest almost touches the floor as you inhale.
Now breathe out and press your upper body back up to the starting position while squeezing your chest.
After a brief pause at the top contracted position, you can begin to lower yourself downward again for as many repetitions as needed.

Slightly bend the knees and place the barbell on your collar bone. Lift the barbell up keeping it lying on your chest. Take a step back and position your feet shoulder width apart from each other.

Once you pick up the barbell with the correct grip length, lift the bar up over your head by locking your arms. Hold at about shoulder level and slightly in front of your head. This is your starting position.
Lower the bar down to the collarbone slowly as you inhale.
Lift the bar back up to the starting position as you exhale.

Clean the dumbbells up one at a time by using your thighs to bring the dumbbells up to shoulder height at each side.
Rotate the wrists so that the palms of your hands are facing forward. This is your starting position.
As you exhale, push the dumbbells up until they touch at the top.
After a second pause, slowly come down back to the starting position as you inhale.

Grab the left pulley with your right hand and the right pulley with your left hand, crossing them in front of you. This will be your starting position.
Initiate the movement by moving your arms back and outward, keeping your arms straight as you execute the movement.
Pause at the end of the motion before returning the handles to the start position.
formCues: Keep your upper arm or torso anchored still so 100% of tension stays on the target muscle.
Pause 0.5–1 second in the peak contraction or stretched position—no momentum.
Use a smooth 2-second eccentric on every single rep, especially the final hard reps.
commonMistakes: Swinging torso or elbows to cheat heavier weight at the expense of target muscle tension.
Letting the cable/machine stack crash at the bottom and losing tension.

name: Pike Push-Up
instructions: Hike hips into an inverted V, lower the crown of your head slightly in front of your hands, and press back up.
setupTip: Bodyweight Setup: Set a clean grip width, brace your abs and glutes into a rigid line, and own a controlled 2-second lowering phase on every rep.
steps: With your back to the wall bend at the waist and place both hands on the floor at shoulder width.

Kick yourself up against the wall with your arms straight. Your body should be upside down with the arms and legs fully extended. Keep your whole body as straight as possible. Tip: If doing this for the first time, have a spotter help you. Also, make sure that you keep facing the wall with your head, rather than looking down.
Slowly lower yourself to the ground as you inhale until your head almost touches the floor. Tip: It is of utmost importance that you come down slow in order to avoid head injury.
Push yourself back up slowly as you exhale until your elbows are nearly locked.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
formCues: Keep shoulder blades depressed and tucked back—never let shoulders shrug toward your ears.
Control the lowering (eccentric) phase for ~2 seconds into a comfortable deep stretch.
Drive smoothly to lockout while exhaling through the sticking point.
commonMistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom stretch or slamming the weight stack between reps.
Flaring elbows straight out at 90° instead of tucking ~30–45° in the scapular plane.

name: Band Bent-Over Row
instructions: Stand on the center of the band, hinge 45° with a flat back, and row handles into your lower ribs.
setupTip: Setup: Establish a stable stance, brace your core 360°, and verify full, pain-free range of motion on your first warm-up rep.
steps: Run a band around a stationary post like that of a squat rack.
Grab the band by the handles and stand back so that the tension in the band rises.

Extend and lift the arms straight in front of you. Tip: Your arms should be straight and parallel to the floor while perpendicular to your torso. Your feet should be firmly planted on the floor spread at shoulder width. This will be your starting position.
As you exhale, move your arms to the sides and back. Keep your arms extended and parallel to the floor. Continue the movement until the arms are extended to your sides.
After a pause, go back to the original position as you inhale.
formCues: Initiate every rep by depressing/gliding your shoulder blades before bending your elbows.
Think of your hands as hooks and drive your elbows back or down toward your hips.
Let your lats/upper back stretch forward under control at the start of each rep.
commonMistakes: Heaving with lower-back momentum to move a stack that's too heavy.
Cutting reps short instead of pulling elbows all the way back and controlling the stretch.

name: Incline Cable Fly
instructions: Set pulleys to bottom, bring handles together in an upward arc, squeeze upper pecs.
setupTip: Set bench at 30 degrees between dual cable pulleys.
steps: Position a bench angled at 30 degrees between two low pulleys.
Grab handles with palms facing up and forward.
Bring hands together in a gentle arc over the upper chest, holding the peak contraction for 1 second.
formCues: Maintain a slight elbow bend throughout the movement.
Keep chest proud and shoulders pinned back.
commonMistakes: Bending and extending elbows turning the fly into a press.

name: Decline Dumbbell Bench Press
instructions: Secure legs on decline bench, lower dumbbells with elbows at 45 degrees, press up over lower chest.
setupTip: Hook ankles securely under rollers before leaning back with weights.
steps: Lie on a decline bench with shins locked under pads.
Press dumbbells directly up, then lower controlled to the lower pecs.
formCues: Tuck elbows at 45 degrees to protect shoulders.
Drive through the sternal head of the pectorals.
commonMistakes: Letting weights drift backward toward the head.

name: Close-Grip Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Grip barbell shoulder-width apart, keep elbows tucked close to ribcage, press explosively through triceps.
setupTip: Avoid ultra-narrow grips that strain wrists; shoulder-width provides optimal triceps recruitment.
steps: Lie flat on bench, grip bar with hands shoulder-width apart.
Lower the bar slowly to lower chest while keeping elbows tucked to torso.
Press upward locking out triceps.
formCues: Elbows should track close to ribs at 30 degrees.
Keep wrists stacked neutral over forearms.
commonMistakes: Placing hands too close (touching), which strains the wrists.

name: Cable Y-Raise
instructions: Cross cables at waist height, raise arms upward and outward into a Y-shape tracking scapular plane.
setupTip: Use cuff attachments or handle-less carabiner grips for unmatched lateral delt isolation.
steps: Set pulleys low, take right cable in left hand and left cable in right hand.
Stand tall, hinge slightly at hips.
Raise arms in a 45-degree high Y shape until hands reach ear height.
formCues: Think about sweeping outward toward the room corners.
Keep traps depressed and relaxed.
commonMistakes: Shrugging up with upper traps instead of side delts.

name: Cable Behind-the-Back Lateral Raise
instructions: Set pulley at hand level, reach behind lower back, raise arm out to the side through full range of motion.
setupTip: Lean slightly away from the cable tower to keep constant tension across the entire excursion.
steps: Stand sideways to cable tower, reach behind back with outside hand to grab handle.
Raise handle laterally until arm is parallel to floor.
formCues: Lead with the elbow and side delt.
Lower with a slow 2-second eccentric.
commonMistakes: Using hip momentum to swing the cable.

name: Cable Glute Kickback
instructions: Attach ankle cuff, hinge at hips, kick leg backward and slightly outward, squeezing glute at top.
setupTip: Angle your working foot slightly outward (30 degrees) to match the glute max muscle fiber orientation.
steps: Attach ankle strap to low cable pulley.
Hinge forward from hips, brace core against machine.
Drive heel back and up, holding peak contraction for 1 second.
formCues: Lock your lower back flat so lumbar doesn't arch.
Initiate strictly from the glute crease.
commonMistakes: Hyperextending lumbar spine instead of extending the hip.

name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
instructions: Rest rear foot on bench, descend front hip straight down until thigh is parallel, push through front midfoot.
setupTip: Position front foot far enough forward so front shin stays near vertical for glutes or forward knee travel for quads.
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand, place laces of rear foot on bench behind you.
Descend until rear knee touches pad or floor gently.
Drive through front heel and midfoot to return to top.
formCues: Keep 85% of weight on front leg.
Keep torso braced with a slight forward lean.
commonMistakes: Pushing off rear toe excessively.

name: Sissy Squat
instructions: Lock shins in sissy bench or hold upright, push knees forward while leaning torso back, stretch quads deeply.
setupTip: Focus on deep knee flexion and maximum rectus femoris stretch at the bottom.
steps: Lock feet under sissy squat pad.
Lean torso back in line with thighs as knees push forward.
Descend until deep quad stretch is felt, then contract quads to stand.
formCues: Maintain straight line from shoulders to knees.
Descend under control.
commonMistakes: Bending at hips (breaking the torso plank).

name: Landmine Press
instructions: Hold end of barbell at shoulder height, press up and forward at a 45-degree angle with a forward lean.
setupTip: Excellent shoulder-friendly alternative for anyone with impingement during overhead or flat bench.
steps: Anchor one end of barbell in corner or landmine sleeve.
Hold top of bar at collarbone height with one or both hands.
Press up and forward until arm is extended.
formCues: Lean slightly forward into the bar as you press.
Keep core braced to prevent torso rotation.
commonMistakes: Leaning backward under heavy weight.

name: Landmine Row
instructions: Straddle barbell, attach V-grip handle under collar, hinge at hips and row bar towards abdomen.
setupTip: Use 25 lb or smaller plates for greater range of motion at the top of the pull.
steps: Straddle bar facing away from anchor point.
Hinge at hips at 45 degrees with flat back.
Pull handle to lower ribs, retracting shoulder blades.
formCues: Pull elbows back past torso.
Hold peak squeeze for 1 second.
commonMistakes: Using torso jerk to swing weight up.

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
instructions: Anchor ankles, lower torso slowly toward floor by resisting with hamstrings, push off floor to return.
setupTip: Focus strictly on the eccentric (lowering) phase for massive hamstring tendon durability and hypertrophy.
steps: Kneel on soft pad with ankles securely anchored under barbell or pad.
Keep hips extended straight, lower body forward as slowly as possible.
Catch yourself on hands and lightly push back up.
formCues: Maintain straight line through hips and torso.
Resist the fall with maximum hamstring tension.
commonMistakes: Hinging hips backward to make the rep easier.

name: Plank
instructions: Rest on forearms and toes, hold rigid straight line from head to heels with posterior pelvic tilt.
setupTip: Squeeze glutes and pull elbows toward toes to double abdominal recruitment.
steps: Place forearms on mat, elbows under shoulders.
Extend legs back on toes, brace abs and glutes.
Hold isometric contraction for target duration.
formCues: Keep hips level, no sagging or piking.
Breathe steadily through diaphragm.
commonMistakes: Sagging lower back into lumbar hyperextension.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
instructions: Hang from pull-up bar, posteriorly tilt pelvis and curl knees up to chest without swinging.
setupTip: Focus on rolling your pelvis upward toward your sternum rather than just flexing hips.
steps: Hang from pull-up bar with overhand grip.
Flex abs and curl pelvis up, pulling knees into chest.
Lower slowly to starting hang.
formCues: Eliminate forward-backward swinging.
Roll pelvis up at top of rep.
commonMistakes: Swinging legs with momentum from hip flexors.

name: Concentration Curl
instructions: Sit on bench, brace triceps against inner thigh, curl dumbbell up to chin with full supination.
setupTip: Bracing arm against inner thigh prevents all body momentum, isolating the biceps peak.
steps: Sit on edge of bench, spread legs.
Rest back of upper arm against inner thigh.
Curl weight up towards face, supinate wrist at peak.
formCues: Keep elbow anchored firmly.
Squeeze peak biceps contraction for 1 second.
commonMistakes: Rocking shoulder backward to swing dumbbell.

name: Reverse Barbell Curl
instructions: Take overhand (pronated) grip on barbell or EZ-bar, curl weight up to chest to build brachioradialis.
setupTip: An EZ-bar reduces wrist strain during pronated curling.
steps: Stand upright, hold barbell with palms facing down (overhand).
Curl bar up by flexing elbows, keeping upper arms pinned to sides.
formCues: Keep wrists straight and neutral.
Feel the contraction in the upper outer forearm.
commonMistakes: Extending wrists backward at top of curl.

name: Forearm Wrist Curl
instructions: Rest forearms on bench or knees with wrists hanging over edge, curl dumbbells upward with wrists.
setupTip: Allow dumbbell to roll gently down to fingers for maximum wrist flexor stretch before curling.
steps: Rest forearms on flat bench with palms facing up, wrists off edge.
Lower weight into fingers, then curl wrists fully upward.
formCues: Keep forearms glued to bench.
Full stretch at bottom, full squeeze at top.
commonMistakes: Lifting forearms off bench.

name: Dumbbell Pullover
instructions: Lie across bench, hold dumbbell with diamond grip over chest, lower back behind head in deep lat stretch.
setupTip: Keep hips low below the bench to increase the stretch on the lats and ribcage.
steps: Position upper back perpendicular across bench.
Hold inner plate of dumbbell with palms forming a diamond.
Lower dumbbell back behind head while keeping slight elbow bend.
Pull through lats and chest to return over torso.
formCues: Feel deep stretch through lats and ribcage.
Pull with armpits rather than pressing with triceps.
commonMistakes: Bending elbows excessively making it a skullcrusher.

name: Outdoor / Treadmill Running
instructions: Cardio endurance and conditioning running session, logged via Apple Watch / Fitness or manually.
setupTip: Log duration, distance, and HR from Apple Watch or Apple Fitness.
steps: Maintain steady upright posture with slight forward lean from ankles.
Strike ground under your center of mass with midfoot landing.
Maintain relaxed shoulder and cadence around 165-175 spm.
formCues: Keep head up and shoulders relaxed.
Breathe rhythmically.
commonMistakes: Overstriding with heavy heel strikes.

name: Soccer / Field Sports
instructions: High-intensity interval conditioning through soccer match or scrimmage.
setupTip: Syncs automatically from Apple Fitness workouts logged on Apple Watch.
steps: Dynamic warm-up and agility footwork before game.
Interval sprints, change of direction, and tactical play.
Cool down walk and hydration post-match.
formCues: Stay light on balls of feet.
Hydrate with electrolytes.
commonMistakes: Skipping warm-up sprints before cold kick-off.

name: Stationary Bike / Cycling
instructions: Low-impact cardiovascular conditioning on spin bike or outdoor cycling.
setupTip: Set saddle height so leg has slight 10-15 degree bend at bottom of pedal stroke.
steps: Adjust seat height to hip bone level.
Pedal at smooth cadence between 80-95 RPM.
Keep upper body relaxed with light grip on handlebars.
formCues: Drive through ball of foot.
Maintain steady cadence.
commonMistakes: Saddle too low causing knee discomfort.

name: Stair Climber
instructions: Continuous vertical step conditioning for intense lower body and aerobic burn.
setupTip: Avoid leaning heavily on the side rails; upright posture maximizes glute recruitment.
steps: Step with whole foot onto revolving stairs.
Drive through heels with upright torso.
Keep hands lightly balancing on rails without supporting bodyweight.
formCues: Push through whole foot, not just toes.
Keep hips tall.
commonMistakes: Hunching forward over rails.

name: Swimming
instructions: Zero-impact full-body cardiovascular training (freestyle, breaststroke, or backstroke).
setupTip: Tracks laps and heart rate seamlessly from Apple Watch in pool.
steps: Streamline body in water with head neutral.
Catch water with high elbow and accelerate pull to hip.
Kick smoothly from hips rather than knees.
formCues: Keep core engaged and body long.
Exhale continuously underwater.
commonMistakes: Lifting head out of water to breathe instead of rotating.
